outcomes.text: Understand the technical principles content as a whole: materials, processes, industry practice, and product development.
Name materials for many uses and justify choices using properties, function, looks, cost, manufacture and disposal.
Link working characteristics such as malleability, toughness, hardness, corrosion resistance and conductivity to material choice.
Classify metals, woods, polymers, papers and boards, composites, smart and modern materials, with examples of each.
Describe workshop and industrial tests for tensile strength, toughness, hardness, malleability, corrosion and conductivity.
Name types of paper and board and describe scoring, cutting, folding, printing, impact and recycling qualities.
Explain which paper or board suits which use, such as cartridge for printing or duplex card for food packaging.
Describe performance of polymer sheet and film such as foam board, fluted polypropylene and plastazote.
Explain why each polymer sheet or film suits a given application.
Name timber stock forms: rough sawn, PSE, PAR, natural, manufactured boards and mouldings.
Describe wood characteristics: grain, warping, shrinkage, splitting, forming, machining and decay resistance.
Recognise common softwoods, hardwoods and manufactured boards and their uses.
Name metal stock forms: sheet, plate, bar, tube and structural sections.
Describe metal characteristics: hardness, elasticity, density, conductivity, melting point, alloying and finishing.
Recognise ferrous, non-ferrous and alloy metals and their uses.
Name polymer stock forms such as sheet, film, granules, rod, foam and powder.
Describe polymer characteristics: toughness, insulation, UV resistance, moulding, chemical resistance and recyclability.
Recognise common thermoplastics and thermosets and their uses.
Explain why elastomers suit given uses and how they improve products such as grips.
Recognise natural rubber, neoprene, silicone and TPE.
Explain how biodegradable polymers degrade and why they suit given uses.
Recognise corn starch polymers, PLA, PHA and water-soluble polymers.
Explain how composites combine materials for better properties, with examples such as CFRP, GRP and reinforced concrete.
Explain smart materials that react to temperature, light or pressure, with examples such as Nitinol and piezo materials.
Explain modern materials such as Kevlar, precious metal clay and polymorph.
Describe how enhancement methods suit given materials and products.
Explain polymer additives such as UV stabilisers and bio-batch for biodegradability.
Explain how resins, lamination, preservatives and finishes improve timber.
Describe heat treatments for metal: case hardening, hardening and tempering.
Describe die cutting, laser cutting, creasing and bending of paper and board.
Describe polymer forming methods such as vacuum forming, injection, blow and rotational moulding and extrusion, and match them to products and scales.
Describe metal forming such as pressing, spinning, deep drawing, forging, rolling and casting, and match them to products.
Describe permanent and temporary metal joining: welding, soldering, brazing, riveting and screws and bolts.
Describe metal wasting processes: milling, turning, flame, plasma and laser cutting, and punching.
Describe wood joints such as dovetail, comb, housing, half-lap, dowel and mortise and tenon, and knock-down fittings.
Describe timber forming: laminating, steam bending, turning, milling and routing.

topics.title: 3.1.4.5 The use of adhesives and fixings

outcomes.text: Know common adhesives: PVA, contact, UV hardening, solvent cement and epoxy.
Explain how jigs and fixtures give accurate repeated manufacture.
Describe finishes for paper and board: laminating, embossing, varnishing and foil blocking.
Compare screen, flexographic, offset lithographic and digital printing for products and scales.
Describe polymer finishes, self-finishing and pigments such as gel coats and smart pigments.
Describe metal finishes that improve looks or prevent corrosion: paints, plating, powder coating, galvanising, anodising.
Describe wood finishes: varnishes, paints, stains, waxes, oils and preservatives.
Describe one-off, batch, mass, unit production, quick response and vertical in-house production with examples.
Relate material cost, form, process and scale; use materials economically and cut waste.
Compare bulk and one-off production savings and explain Just In Time manufacture.
Explain how computer systems plan production: modular cells, JIT, QRM and flexible systems.
Explain computer controlled production, distribution, storage and bought-in standard components.
Explain sub-assembly as a separate manufacturing line.
Compare CAD with manual drawing and describe 2D and 3D CAD uses.
Describe CAM processes: laser cutting, routing, milling, turning and plotter cutting.
Describe simulation, CFD and FEA testing before production.
Explain rapid prototyping and 3D printing and their benefits.
Describe EPOS for stock and customer data, and PPC networking for materials, scheduling and suppliers.

topics.title: 3.1.8 The requirements for product design and development

outcomes.text: Analyse existing products for fitness for purpose, accuracy and meeting specifications, to propose new designs.
Consider aesthetics, ergonomics and anthropometrics when designing for a target market.
Explain inclusive design for disabled, child and elderly users.
Explain the Health and Safety at Work Act, COSHH, workshop hazards and risk assessment.
Explain consumer safety: consumer legislation, BSI testing, toy safety marks and instructions and warnings.
Explain copyright, design rights, patents, registered designs, trademarks and logos.
Explain open design and examples such as humanitarian projects and shared 3D print files.

topics.title: 3.1.11 Design for manufacturing, maintenance, repair and disposal

outcomes.text: Modify designs to cut processes, label materials, ease disassembly and apply the six Rs.
Design for maintenance with standard parts, repairable fixings and software upgrades.
Explain ease-of-manufacture features: ribs, snap fittings, screw posts, standard parts and self-finishing.
Explain designing for disassembly, including integral fixings and smart materials.
Explain how feasibility studies and consumer prototype testing assess practicality of production.

topics.title: 3.1.13 Enterprise and marketing in the development of products

outcomes.text: Explain brand identity: customers, labelling, packaging, corporate identity and global marketing.
Explain product costing, profit and the role of entrepreneurs.
Explain collaborative design work, virtual and face to face.
Present proposals using reports, graphs, tables, sketches, rendering and dimensioned manufacturing detail.
Understand designing and making principles as a whole: methods, theory, responsible design and project management.
Explain user centred design that meets needs, wants and values with no single fixed process.
Use market research, interviews, focus groups, product analysis, anthropometric and ergonomic data.
Develop a proposal, plan and make a prototype, and evaluate it to refine the design.
Discuss how historical styles, movements and designers shaped products.
Discuss arts and crafts, Art Deco, Modernism and Post modernism principles.
Discuss Starck, Dyson, Calvert, Rams, the Eameses and Brandt and their movements.

topics.title: 3.2.3 How technology and cultural changes can impact on the work of designers

outcomes.text: Discuss socio-economic influences: Bauhaus, wartime utility goods and modern mass-produced furniture.
Discuss how microelectronics, new materials and CAD/CAM shape design.
Discuss sustainable, ethical, culturally acceptable and inclusive products, social problems and Fairtrade.
Describe introduction, growth, maturity, decline and replacement, and how designers redevelop products.
Carry out design stages: analysis, mood boards, ideas, illustration, specification, modelling, planning and testing.
Develop a prototype from design proposals for identified users.
Describe how companies use collaborative, cyclic design methods.
Critique own and commercial products to suggest improvements.
Describe rigorous testing of commercial products before sale.
Use third party feedback objectively to guide further development.

topics.title: 3.2.6 Selecting appropriate tools, equipment and processes

outcomes.text: Choose correct tools and safe workshop practice for tasks.
Explain scaling from prototype to batch and mass manufacture, and picking suitable processes.
Explain commercial health and safety, training and national standards.
Explain how testing, templates, jigs and fixtures keep production accurate and reduce human error.
Discuss sustainable materials and the environmental impact of packaging.
Explain the circular economy, minimising energy, waste, extraction impact and product miles, and the costs of waste.

topics.title: 3.2.9 Design for manufacture and project management

outcomes.text: Plan for accuracy and efficiency in prototypes and for small, medium and large production runs.
Explain quality assurance systems: TQM, scrum, Six Sigma and critical path analysis.
Explain quality control: tolerance checks, go-no go gauges, scanning, vernier callipers, micrometers and non-destructive testing.

topics.title: 3.2.10 National and international standards in product design

outcomes.text: Explain standards: BSI, ISO, RoHS, battery, packaging and WEEE directives.
Explain polymer recycling codes, energy ratings and eco-labels such as Mobius Loop, FSC and Energy Star.
